Fold-change in AUC due to food effect on oral absorption, as reported in clinical pharmacology studies or labels. A value of 1 indicates no food effect; values greater than 1 indicate increased exposure with food.

Number of Lipinski rule-of-five violations (molecular weight > 500, logP > 5, hydrogen-bond donors > 5, hydrogen-bond acceptors > 10) computed from the compound structure; lower counts indicate better oral drug-likeness and absorption potential. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by median.

Computed XLogP (log units) from PubChem. The source states moderate lipophilicity (logP ≈ 2–4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors; candidates are ranked by distance outside this band, with values inside the band scoring best.

Molecular weight of the compound in Daltons (g/mol), computed from structure by the curated descriptor route rather than a trained prediction; lower values are preferred because size above roughly 500 Da approaches the upper limit compatible with efficient passive intestinal diffusion and increases efflux-transporter recognition.

Whether the compound is documented as orally administered in humans (e.g., approved oral drug, clinical trial oral dosing). This is a preference, not a requirement: absence of documentation gives unknown, never fail, because the oral route may simply be undocumented.

Reported absolute or relative oral bioavailability (F%) in humans, as a measured pharmacokinetic parameter. Higher values indicate greater fraction of an orally administered dose reaching systemic circulation intact. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: low F% compounds may still be clinically effective if the dose can be escalated.

Model-predicted probability of blood-brain barrier penetration; lower probability is generally preferred for peripheral targets to minimise CNS side effects.

ADMET-AI ClinTox model output: predicted probability in [0,1] of clinical toxicity. The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents general toxicity and dose-limiting adverse events for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.
Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP1A2, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C19, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.
Model-predicted probability that the compound inhibits CYP2C9, in [0,1]; higher values indicate greater drug-drug interaction liability.

The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents CYP3A4-mediated drug-drug interaction liability for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold.

The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents CYP3A4 substrate liability for this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold.

The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents hepatotoxicity as a frequent, dose-limiting liability of this drug class but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher probability is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence documents QT-prolongation events for kinase inhibitors and asserts off-target hERG inhibition for a drug class, but no cited claim validates this model or states a probability threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

The catalog documents the endpoint, its unit and its direction (higher clearance is worse). Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence establishes that metabolic stability is a development criterion and reports measured hepatocyte clearance values that fix the direction, but no cited claim validates this model or states a numeric threshold. Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the median is recorded.

Predicted probability that a compound is absorbed from the human gastrointestinal tract, from the ADMET-AI HIA_Hou classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted intestinal absorption.

Model-predicted lipophilicity (logP) from the ADMET-AI Lipophilicity_AstraZeneca regression endpoint, in log units. The cited heuristic states that moderate lipophilicity (typically logP approximately 2-4) is optimal for kinase inhibitors, facilitating passive membrane diffusion without excessively compromising aqueous solubility. Candidates within this range rank higher than those outside it.
Model-predicted logP (RDKit); lower values are preferred because lipophilic, poorly soluble agents show food-dependent and variable oral absorption.

Recorded as an exploratory consideration only: the cited evidence establishes that metabolic stability is a development criterion and reports measured clearance values that fix the direction, but no cited claim validates this model or states a numeric threshold. Predicted probability that a compound achieves oral bioavailability in humans, from the ADMET-AI Bioavailability_Ma classifier. Values in [0,1]; higher values indicate better predicted oral exposure.

ADMET-AI Pgp_Broccatelli classifier output: predicted probability in [0,1] that the compound inhibits P-glycoprotein; higher values indicate greater predicted P-gp inhibition, which can alter absorption, distribution and drug-drug interaction liability. Values pooled from the contributing sources are reduced by max, so the least favourable prediction governs.
Number of PAINS alerts from RDKit; higher counts indicate greater likelihood of assay interference and poor drug-likeness.

Criterion: Predicted plasma protein binding rate (ADMET-AI PPBR_AZ, %)

Where several predicted values are available for a compound, the worst-case (maximum) value is recorded.

Criterion: Predicted volume of distribution at steady state
Definition: Model-predicted volume of distribution (L/kg); affects tissue distribution and potential for toxicity.
Number of rotatable bonds, computed from the structure. Lower values indicate reduced molecular flexibility, which is generally associated with improved passive diffusion and oral bioavailability.

Criterion: Time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax, median of reported values)
Definition: Median of reported times to maximum plasma concentration after oral administration, in hours; when a source reports only a range, the range midpoint is used. Lower values indicate faster absorption. This is a preference ordering, not a requirement: longer Tmax may still be compatible with oral bioavailability and efficacy.

Topological polar surface area in Å² computed from the compound's structure by the PubChem computed-descriptor route (derived, not a trained prediction). Lower values are associated with enhanced passive diffusion, and values at or below approximately 90 Å² lie in the low-polarity band the cited source links to improved penetration; the criterion is applied as a preference favouring oral absorption. Where a compound carries values from more than one source record, the pooled value is the median across them.
